record.notes: Announced 3 Jun 2025; the centre is part of NIST. After EO 14434 of 29 Sep 2026 (US-26), NIST presents it as the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) and its mandate refers to 'SI' systems, while its news items still use the name CAISI. Its published work includes the NIST AI 800-2 draft on automated benchmark evaluations (Jan 2026, US-21); evaluations of DeepSeek V4 Pro (1 May 2026), Z.ai's GLM-5.2 (17 Jul 2026) and GLM-5.3's cyber capabilities (17 Sep 2026); a preliminary assessment of Kimi K3's cyber capabilities with the UK AI Security Institute (23 Jul 2026); and key practices for incident readiness and response in SI training and evaluation (16 Oct 2026). America's AI Action Plan (Jul 2025, US-16) assigns it tasks that include evaluating frontier models. The House 'Great American AI Act' discussion draft (Jun 2026) would codify the centre; it has not been enacted.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: the official source, the commerce.gov statement of 3 Jun 2025, again could not be stored (HTTP 403 Forbidden; the browser retry timed out), so the title and date_published rest on the record's earlier verification of 11 Oct 2026, when the statement was read but not stored. Stored: NIST's centre page (nist.gov/caissi), on 11 Oct and again on 17 Oct 2026, and in this run NIST's super intelligence page (nist.gov/super-intelligence). The centre page confirms the CAISSI name, the mandate in the summary (now worded for 'SI' systems), the voluntary character of its agreements and standards, and the evaluations in notes (DeepSeek V4 Pro on the 11 Oct copy; the 16 Oct 2026 incident-readiness practices on the 17 Oct copy). The super intelligence page confirms that NIST does this work through CAISSI and that NIST is updating its communications under EO 14434 of 29 Sep 2026. The 30 Sep 2026 date in date_last_updated appears only in the centre page's metadata (article modified time), not in its text. The tasks in America's AI Action Plan rest on US-16's stored plan, the NIST AI 800-2 draft on US-21, and the Great American AI Act draft on US-25. Press reports (GovConWire, Sep 2026) say the centre signed pre- and post-release testing agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI; no stored official source confirms this.

changes.notes: rewritten: the remark that the testing agreements reported by GovConWire could not be confirmed is research-process language and moved to verification.note; adds the 16 Oct 2026 incident-readiness practices now listed on the NIST page and the AI Action Plan's tasks, and names the records that other statements rest on

judgment.status_reasoning: The NIST page stored on 17 Oct 2026 still states the centre's mandate in the future tense of the original statement ('will serve as industry's primary point of contact ... CAISSI will:') under its new name, and lists work published up to 16 Oct 2026. Nothing in the stored files shows the mandate withdrawn; the renaming after EO 14434 changed the name and the wording ('SI' for 'AI'), not the functions. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Mandate of a national AI testing and standards body that succeeded the US AI Safety Institute; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: No stored file gives the statement's date (3 Jun 2025). For the renaming, the super intelligence page gives only the date of the executive order behind it (29 Sep 2026); the centre page's own modification date, 30 Sep 2026, is in its metadata, not its text. date_published and date_last_updated stay as published (see open_questions).
judgment.summary_reasoning: The summary's mandate list matches the six functions on the stored NIST page (which also names OSTP among the coordination partners). Its opening clause, that the statement reorganises the US AI Safety Institute as CAISI, rests on the title of the unstored commerce.gov statement. Left unchanged.

extra_urls.why: NIST page linked from the stored centre page (menu 'Super intelligence'); the record's earlier verification read it as confirming that the renaming to CAISSI was made under EO 14434. Storing it may give a citable date for date_last_updated and support the renaming in notes.
